name: Roast Duckling
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: almonds, blanched and chopped very fine

instructions.text: Whip three tablespoonfuls of mashed potatoes to a white cream with butter and a tablespoonful of cream
Season with celery salt and white pepper
Add three tablespoonfuls of almonds, blanched and chopped very fine
Stuff your young ducks when you have cleaned and washed them with this mixture
Do not distend the bodies, but fill without packing
Truss and bind legs and wings into position with cotton-twine
Lay the plump creatures upon the grating of your roaster
Rub the breast with a split onion
Dust with pepper, salt and flour
Put a cupful of boiling water into the pan and cover
Set in a very quick oven for the first fifteen minutes
Change, then, to a more moderate, and cook, still covered, ten minutes to the pound
Uncover, baste well with gravy, then with butter
Skim the fat from the gravy
Thicken with a tablespoonful of browned flour, rubbed up with two tablespoonfuls of currant jelly, and send to table in a boat

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Whip three tablespoonfuls of mashed potatoes to a white cream with butter and a tablespoonful of cream
2. Season with celery salt and white pepper
3. Add three tablespoonfuls of almonds, blanched and chopped very fine
4. Stuff your young ducks when you have cleaned and washed them with this mixture
5. Do not distend the bodies, but fill without packing
6. Truss and bind legs and wings into position with cotton-twine
7. Lay the plump creatures upon the grating of your roaster
8. Rub the breast with a split onion
9. Dust with pepper, salt and flour
10. Put a cupful of boiling water into the pan and cover
11. Set in a very quick oven for the first fifteen minutes
12. Change, then, to a more moderate, and cook, still covered, ten minutes to the pound
13. Uncover, baste well with gravy, then with butter
14. Dredge with flour, and brown
15. Skim the fat from the gravy
16. Thicken with a tablespoonful of browned flour, rubbed up with two tablespoonfuls of currant jelly, and send to table in a boat
